title: What If a Carrington Solar Storm Hit Today?

scenes.text: What if a Carrington storm hit today? In eighteen fifty nine it set telegraph paper on fire.
The warning would be short. In eighteen fifty nine the blast crossed to Earth in about seventeen hours.
Within minutes, long power lines pick up surges. In nineteen eighty nine a weaker storm blacked out Quebec for about nine hours.
Satellites could be damaged, taking GPS, phones and radio with them, and repairs could take weeks or longer.
Researchers at Lloyd's estimated damage to the United States alone at roughly six hundred billion to two and a half trillion dollars.
Storms this big come about every five hundred years, and nobody can predict when the next one arrives.

description:
What if a Carrington solar storm hit today?
In 1859 it shocked telegraph operators. Today it could damage power grids and satellites, with US losses estimated in the trillions.
